newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toray first-half group profit up more than 50%.
newsitem.headline: Toray first-half group profit up more than 50%.

text.p: Interim profits at Japan's top maker of synthetic fibres, Toray Industries Inc, jumped by more than 50 percent on a group basis as a result of active investment by the firm in its units.
"Investments in our units have started to bear fruit. All of our units, at home and abroad, increased their sales handsomely," a company spokesman said.
Toray announced on Thursday that it posted group sales of 501.22 billion yen ($4.51 billion) in the half year to September 30, up 10.3 percent from a year ago.
It said it enjoyed a sales increase of more than 10 percent in almost all its business divisions.
As a result, the company's group net profit was 11.88 billion yen ($107 million) in the six-month period, up 51.9 percent from a year ago.
The company has diversified into plastics, chemicals, housing, pharmaceuticals and electronics-related products.
It has been trying to expand its business as a group and it has been actively investing in its units, the spokesman said.
Toray said its parent company current profit in the half-year period was 17.12 billion yen ($154 million), up 5.1 percent from the same period a year ago.

Current profit is pre-tax but includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities. Net profit is obtained by subtracting special profit and income tax from current profit.

For the full 1996/97 year to March 31, Toray forecast a group net profit of 25 billion yen ($225 million), up more than 37 percent from the previous year. It expects a full-year parent current profit of 40 billion yen ($360 million), up just over 10 percent. ($1=111)
